privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: AI Menu APP helps users translate and understand restaurant menus from photos, files, documents, and menu links. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices available to users.

sections.heading: Information we collect
items: Account information, such as username, email address, optional phone number, and authentication identifiers.
Profile preferences, such as dietary preferences, allergies, budget, and taste preferences when users choose to provide them.
User-provided menu content, including menu photos, PDFs, documents, text, webpages, and delivery app share links.
Generated menu results, including translated dish names, descriptions, ingredients, allergens, prices, menu history, and order list items.
Technical data such as app interactions, diagnostics, device or advertising identifiers, and network request metadata.

sections.heading: How we use information

To save account profiles, menu history, and order list data for signed-in users.
To improve reliability, prevent abuse, debug errors, and maintain app security.
To show advertising and measure ad performance where ads are enabled.

home.title: Understand a menu before you order
paragraphs: AI Menu APP is designed for travelers and diners who need more context than a word-for-word translation. It combines text extraction, menu structure detection, and translation so sections, dish names, descriptions, and prices remain easier to compare.

Menu photos and documents vary widely. Lighting, decorative fonts, multiple columns, handwritten notes, and mixed languages can all affect recognition. Clear, straight images and complete PDF pages usually produce the most useful result.

The translated menu is a reading aid, not a replacement for the restaurant's current menu or staff. Always confirm prices, availability, ingredients, and allergy information directly with the restaurant before ordering.

faq.question: Which menu formats can I use?
faq.answer: You can submit a menu photo, image file, PDF, or public menu webpage. Password-protected documents and pages that block automated access may not be readable.

faq.question: How can I improve recognition?
faq.answer: Capture the full page in focus, avoid glare and steep angles, and keep prices beside their dish names. For multi-page menus, use the original PDF when available.

faq.question: Are translations guaranteed to be accurate?
faq.answer: No. OCR and AI translation can misread stylized text, regional dish names, abbreviations, or unusual layouts. Compare important details with the source menu and ask restaurant staff when uncertain.

faq.question: Can I rely on allergen or dietary labels?
faq.answer: No. Recipes and kitchen practices can change, and cross-contact may not appear on a menu. People with allergies or medical dietary restrictions should confirm directly with the restaurant.

faq.question: What happens to submitted menu content?
faq.answer: Menu content is sent to the cloud and AI services needed to perform the requested analysis. Retention, account choices, and service providers are explained in the Privacy Policy.

howItWorks.title: How AI Menu APP reads a menu
howItWorks.summary: A practical explanation of the steps from a photo, PDF, or webpage to an organized translated menu, including the limits users should check before ordering.

sections.heading: 1. Capture or provide the menu
paragraphs: The process begins with the source that best preserves the restaurant's information. A digital PDF is usually preferable to a screenshot because it can retain sharper text and complete pages. For a printed menu, a straight photo with even lighting reduces missing lines and incorrect characters.
A public link may contain text, a linked PDF, or images. Some sites load content dynamically or block automated access, so a file upload can be more reliable when a link cannot be read.
items: Include the complete page and avoid cutting off headings or prices.
Use one clear source instead of repeatedly compressed screenshots.
Remove unrelated receipts and personal information from the frame.

sections.heading: 2. Recover text and menu structure
paragraphs: Text extraction identifies visible words while the parser separates restaurant information, headings, dish names, descriptions, and prices. Layout matters because a number beside a dish is usually a price, while a large label above several dishes is more likely a category.

Menus often mix languages, currencies, serving sizes, and decorative text. Language profiles and general menu patterns help, but unusual typography or missing context can still produce the wrong grouping.
items: Review category boundaries on multi-column menus.
Check decimal marks and currency symbols carefully.
Compare repeated size prices with the original layout.

sections.heading: 3. Translate and verify
paragraphs: Dish names and descriptions are translated after the structure is recovered. Familiar culinary terms may be preserved when a literal translation would be misleading, while descriptions provide context for ingredients and preparation.
Regional names, handwritten changes, and culturally specific dishes may require clarification from restaurant staff. Keep the original wording available so staff can identify the exact item.
items: Confirm final prices and availability with the restaurant.
Treat ingredient and allergen information as incomplete unless confirmed.
Report repeatable recognition problems with the source and language pair.

guide.title: A practical guide to translating restaurant menus
guide.summary: How to prepare a menu image, interpret translated dish information, and make safer ordering decisions when dining in another language.

sections.heading: Choose the clearest source
paragraphs: Start with the original menu PDF or webpage when possible. For a photo, hold the camera parallel to the page and make sure small descriptions and prices are readable before uploading. Process long menus as complete pages in their natural order so headings keep their context.
items: Avoid shadows and glare across price columns.
Keep currency notes, portion legends, and footnotes visible.
Select the source language manually when automatic detection is wrong.

sections.heading: Read the result with context
paragraphs: A dish name alone may not explain what arrives at the table. Read the original name, translation, description, section, and price together. Preparation words such as grilled, cured, raw, braised, or fried often matter as much as the main ingredient.
items: Check whether ingredients are complete or only highlights.
Look for per-person, market-price, minimum-order, and service-charge notes.
Confirm whether optional additions change the displayed price.

sections.heading: Handle dietary restrictions carefully
paragraphs: A translated menu cannot observe recipe substitutions, shared fryers, or cross-contact. Use the translation to prepare specific questions, then show the original dish name to staff. For serious allergies or medical restrictions, direct restaurant confirmation is essential.
items: Ask about sauces, stocks, marinades, and garnishes.
Ask whether shared equipment creates cross-contact risk.
Do not rely on a generated dietary label as a safety guarantee.

sections.heading: Check prices before choosing a dish
paragraphs: Price columns often contain more than one number. A pair such as 9 / 14 may describe two portion sizes, while +3 usually marks an optional addition rather than the complete dish price. Labels such as market price, per person, minimum two people, and service included change how the number should be read.

Keep each number beside the original dish while reviewing the translation. If a price is missing, attached to a heading, or shown without its qualifier, return to the source instead of guessing from nearby items.
items: Match currency symbols and decimal separators to the menu's locale.
Preserve size labels such as cup, bowl, half, whole, glass, and bottle.
Confirm taxes, service charges, and minimum orders with the restaurant.

sections.heading: Review the result in five steps
paragraphs: Before ordering, compare the translated result with the source in a fixed order: section heading, dish name, description, price, and footnotes. This catches common layout mistakes faster than rereading the translated menu alone.
items: Count source dishes and translated dishes in each section.
Check the first and last item in every column or page.
Look for symbols explained only in a legend or footer.

languages.title: Supported menu languages
languages.summary: AI Menu APP supports twelve source and target languages, with language-aware handling for scripts, punctuation, menu terms, and common price formats.

sections.heading: Available languages
paragraphs: The current set includes English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Portuguese, German, Italian, and Arabic. Automatic detection is available when the source language is unknown.
Menus may contain borrowed culinary terms or multiple languages. Selecting the main language manually can improve consistency when a restaurant name or translated subtitle is visually dominant.
items: Chinese processing accepts Simplified and Traditional menu content.
Arabic right-to-left text can be affected by complex mixed-number layouts.
Japanese and Korean menus often mix local scripts, Latin names, and numbers.

sections.heading: Why language-aware parsing matters
paragraphs: Languages use different punctuation, spacing, currency placement, counters, and portion terms. Shared rules handle general menu structure while language profiles provide script and price context without restaurant-specific exceptions.
items: Keep currency symbols and decimal separators visible.
Preserve vertical text and reading order on East Asian menus.
Include headings that explain fixed-price menus, sizes, or portions.

sections.heading: Translation direction and quality
paragraphs: Any supported source language can be translated into another supported target language. Quality varies with image clarity, layout, regional vocabulary, and available context, so important ordering details must be checked against the source.
items: Use the original dish name when asking restaurant staff a question.
Retry with a clearer source when many items or prices are missing.
Send feedback for repeatable language or layout problems.

about.title: About AI Menu APP
about.summary: AI Menu APP is a menu-reading tool built to help diners understand unfamiliar dishes while keeping the original menu available for verification.

sections.heading: Why the project exists
paragraphs: Restaurant menus carry context that ordinary sentence translation can miss. A useful tool must preserve sections, dish names, descriptions, and prices together so diners can compare choices instead of reading disconnected words.
AI Menu APP focuses on that practical task and returns an organized result that can be reviewed alongside the original wording.
items: Help travelers understand local dishes before ordering.
Keep original names visible for communication with staff.
Explain limitations instead of presenting generated results as guaranteed facts.

sections.heading: How the service is developed
paragraphs: The service combines document extraction, OCR, menu structure parsing, translation, and optional dish information. Quality work includes testing real layouts, checking missing items and prices, and improving language-specific behavior without restaurant-specific hardcoding.
items: Recognition changes are tested across multiple menu formats.
User-facing and legal text is maintained in supported languages.
Security credentials and private account data are not published in code.

sections.heading: Responsible use
paragraphs: The service supports understanding and communication, but it does not control restaurant recipes, prices, availability, or preparation. Generated dish images may be illustrative and may not show the restaurant's actual presentation.
items: Do not treat generated allergy information as a safety guarantee.
Do not assume a matched image represents the exact dish.
Consult the Privacy Policy for data handling and account choices.

sections.heading: Product and recognition feedback
paragraphs: For recognition problems, include the source type, selected languages, and which sections, dishes, or prices were missing or grouped incorrectly. A public menu URL is useful when it remains available. Remove personal data unrelated to the menu problem.
items: Describe the expected result and the result received.

paragraphs: Privacy questions and deletion requests use the same support address. Account deletion requests should come from the registered email so ownership can be verified. Never email passwords, tokens, payment card numbers, government identifiers, or medical records.
items: Use the Account Deletion page for the recommended format.

paragraphs: Support can investigate reproducible application behavior and explain account controls. It cannot confirm a restaurant's recipe, ingredient sourcing, preparation, availability, final bill, reservation, or refund.
items: Use the original dish name when contacting a restaurant.
Keep receipts for questions involving payment or availability.
Seek qualified medical advice for health-related dietary decisions.

examples.title: Worked menu translation examples
examples.summary: Concrete examples showing how dish names, descriptions, categories, and prices should stay connected when a menu is translated.

sections.heading: Example 1: a Spanish tapas section
paragraphs: Consider a section headed PARA COMPARTIR with three lines: Pan con tomate 6,50; Gambas al ajillo 14; and Pulpo a la gallega 18. The heading means dishes intended for sharing, not a dish with its own price. Each number belongs to the dish on the same line, and the comma in 6,50 is a decimal separator.

A useful English result keeps the section as To Share and renders the dishes as Tomato Bread, Garlic Shrimp, and Galician-style Octopus while preserving 6.50, 14, and 18 beside the correct items. The original Spanish names should remain visible because they are the clearest way to point out the order to staff.
items: Category: PARA COMPARTIR becomes To Share.
Dish: Pan con tomate keeps the price 6,50.
Dish: Gambas al ajillo keeps the price 14.
Dish: Pulpo a la gallega keeps the price 18.

sections.heading: Example 2: a Simplified Chinese noodle menu
paragraphs: Now consider a heading 面食 followed by 红烧牛肉面 ¥38, 番茄鸡蛋面 ¥30, and 加面 +¥6. The heading identifies a noodle section. The first two lines are complete dishes, while 加面 is an add-on for an extra portion of noodles and should not be presented as a standalone main dish.

An English translation can organize the entries as Braised Beef Noodles at ¥38 and Tomato and Egg Noodles at ¥30, with Extra Noodles +¥6 clearly marked as an add-on. The plus sign is essential context: dropping it changes the meaning of the price.
items: Category: 面食 becomes Noodles or Noodle Dishes.
Dish: 红烧牛肉面 remains associated with ¥38.
Dish: 番茄鸡蛋面 remains associated with ¥30.
Add-on: 加面 preserves the +¥6 qualifier.

sections.heading: Price patterns that need context
paragraphs: Menus use compact price notation to save space. The same digits can represent a price, a choice of sizes, a supplement, a quantity, or part of a set-menu rule. Layout and nearby labels must be considered together before assigning a number to a dish.
items: 14 / 22 can mean small and large, glass and bottle, or two portion sizes.
MP or market price means the current price must be confirmed with the restaurant.
+3 is usually a supplement and must remain linked to the option it modifies.
12,50 € and $12.50 use different symbol placement and decimal conventions.
45 per person may require a minimum party size stated elsewhere on the menu.

sections.heading: How to review an automated result
paragraphs: Start by checking completeness rather than wording. Compare the number of categories and dishes, then inspect price placement and only then refine translations. A fluent dish name is not useful if it belongs to the wrong section or carries another item's price.

Finally, verify ingredient and dietary claims against the original description. A menu may list only notable ingredients, and neither OCR nor translation can reveal substitutions, shared equipment, or cross-contact that the restaurant did not publish.
items: Check that every source category has a corresponding result section.
Check that each visible source dish appears exactly once.
Check that prices, size labels, and add-ons remain attached to the correct dish.
Keep the original wording available for restaurant staff.
Ask the restaurant to confirm allergies, availability, and the final bill.
